name: Alfacalcidol
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Alfacalcidol (1-alpha-hydroxyvitamin D3) is converted in the liver to calcitriol, bypassing the kidney's 1-alpha-hydroxylation step, so it is a kidney-indicated drug (uremic bone disease, secondary hyperparathyroidism). The Irish label titrates the dose to calcium, phosphate and parathyroid hormone (PTH) and gives an after-dialysis intermittent regimen. Hypercalcemia is the main risk. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Not renally cleared; dose titrated to calcium, phosphate and PTH. Bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: No kidney dose adjustment: alfacalcidol is designed for impaired renal 1-alpha-hydroxylation. Start 1 microgram/day (0.5 microgram in older adults); usual maintenance 0.25 to 2 micrograms/day, titrated to calcium, phosphate, PTH and alkaline phosphatase (SmPC). Add a phosphate binder in renal bone disease.
bands.short: 1 mcg/day start; titrate to Ca, PTH

bands.recommendation: KDIGO 2017: not for routine use in CKD G3a–G5 not on dialysis; reserve for severe, progressive secondary hyperparathyroidism (mainly G4–G5). If used: SmPC start 1 microgram/day (0.5 microgram in older adults), maintenance 0.25 to 2 micrograms/day, titrated to calcium, phosphate and PTH; stop for hypercalcemia.

hd.text: Daily dosing as above, or intermittent dosing after each dialysis (2 to 3 times weekly): start 0.5 to 2 micrograms, adjust by 0.25 to 0.5 microgram steps by PTH, calcium and phosphate. Converting daily to intermittent: daily dose × 7/3 (three times weekly) or × 7/2 (twice weekly), rounded to 0.25 microgram (SmPC).

pd.text: Daily dosing titrated to calcium, phosphate and PTH (SmPC).

crrt.text: No CRRT-specific guidance; usually held in acute illness. Specialist input.

dialyzable: Not stated. In overdose, hemodialysis with low-calcium dialysate can treat hypercalcemia (SmPC 4.9).
monitoring: Serum calcium and phosphate regularly; PTH, alkaline phosphatase and calcium × phosphate product as indicated. If hypercalcemia occurs, stop until calcium normalizes (about 1 week), then restart at half the dose. Hypercalcemia can worsen kidney function and cause nephrocalcinosis (SmPC 4.4). In CKD, check calcium and phosphate often during titration and after each dose change, and PTH at the intervals in the KDIGO CKD-MBD guideline; prefer non-calcium phosphate binders if calcium is high-normal.

pediatric.usual_dose: Over 20 kg: 1 microgram/day. Under 20 kg: 0.05 microgram/kg/day. Neonates and premature infants: 0.05 to 0.1 microgram/kg/day (up to 2 micrograms/kg/day in severe neonatal hypocalcemia) (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Dose by weight and titrated to calcium, phosphate and PTH (SmPC).

adult: CKD G3–G5 tiles amber 'not routine (KDIGO 2017 rec 4.2.2)', matching the approved calcitriol monograph; ≥60 green (hypoparathyroidism, rickets indications).

revision_log.change: CKD G3–G5 not on dialysis: amber 'Not routine (KDIGO)'; band text gives KDIGO 2017 rec 4.2.2 and the SmPC dose if used.

Monitoring: frequent calcium/phosphate checks during titration, PTH per KDIGO CKD-MBD intervals; non-calcium binders if calcium high-normal. Specific week/month intervals in the proposal were not published (not verifiable in the SmPC or the KDIGO executive summary).
